name: InvoiceBatch — Batch Invoice PDFs from a Spreadsheet, Totals Reconciled (Local, Private)
description:
All my invoice data is already in a spreadsheet — what turns it into finished invoice PDFs in one batch? What you don't have is a free afternoon to turn 200 rows into 200 correct invoices — or to find out which totals in that sheet are quietly wrong.
InvoiceBatch takes one spreadsheet of invoice lines (.csv / .xlsx, one row per line item), generates one print-ready PDF per invoice plus a combined file, and reconciles every cent: each line amount, subtotal, tax and total is recomputed from the lines with exact decimal arithmetic before anything is rendered.
WHAT IT CORRECTS ON ITS OWN
• Stated totals that disagree with their own lines — the recomputed value is used and the correction is logged (old → new, with the reason)
• Dates written as 5 Mar 2026 or 05/03/2026 — normalized to ISO format
WHAT IT REPORTS — BUT NEVER SILENTLY CHANGES
• The same invoice number used for two different clients
• Invoices with no client name
• Negative-quantity lines
• Gaps in your invoice number sequence
Then it RE-CHECKS: every total is recomputed a second time, independently, and compared against what went into the PDFs — to the cent.
VERIFIED, NOT VIBES
On a seeded 9-line test sheet (6 invoices, 5 planted defects): 3 corrections applied and logged — including a stated total of 330.00 that recomputed to 385.00 — 4 items flagged for a human decision (3 of them blocking), and the independent re-check matched all 6 invoice totals with 0 mismatches. Grand total across the batch: 1,467.00, to the cent.
100% LOCAL & PRIVATE — no upload, no account, no subscription. Your client list and pricing never leave your computer.
Windows 10/11, no other software needed. You get the invoice PDFs (one per invoice + one combined file) and the reconciliation report.
Scope: InvoiceBatch recomputes arithmetic and checks numbering. It does not judge whether your prices, tax rates or client details are the right ones — and it does not send, collect or chase payments.
